plan.english: Elder, the assembly sat down yesterday. The warriors want war, and the old men want peace. What do you counsel? Young one, war devours the livestock. Have you seen a burning village? I have not seen one. The enemies do steal our cattle by night. Then send a man to their chief, and ask for payment. If they do not give it, the young men will speak. Then I will send my brother.

I will stay, and I will build the fence.

title: How to speak before the people

plan.english: Grandfather, teach me! How shall I speak in the assembly? Listen to the old men, and be silent. And when shall I speak? Speak when your heart is full. Say true words, and the people will hear you. And if I deceive them? Then no one will trust your speech. A lie is a thief. Do you know this, child? I know it, grandfather.

plan.english: Father, your breath is weak. What shall I do for you? My days are few. Hear me, and remember this. I am listening. Guard the peace with the people of the river. Their grandfather and I made a pledge. And if their young men break the pledge? Then go to their assembly, and do not go to war. I will remember it.

plan.english: By which of the two paths shall we go? The path by the water is long; the path over the mountain is dangerous. Why is it dangerous? Wolves dwell in the rocks, and last year they took two sheep. The sheep will grow tired on the long path. Tired sheep live, and the wolf does not eat them. You are right, friend. We will go by the long path.

Give him water, and let him sit by the hearth. And if he steals our goats by night? The dogs are watchful. Do not be afraid, wife.

title: The old men by the fire

plan.english: Grandfather, why do the old men sit by the fire through the night? They are deciding the boundary. A man is speaking, and the others listen. When will they decide? When it dawns, they will decide. Lie down, child, and sleep. I will stay awake, and I will listen.

plan.english: Old men, how many cows shall we give to the kin of the dead man? The payment for a man is a hundred cows. Our herd is not great. Then give seven bulls and a foal. And a boy of yours will shepherd their sheep for a year. And will his kin keep the peace? They gave a pledge in the assembly. They will not break it. Then we will drive them in the morning.

title: The king's word to the herdsmen

plan.english: You come from the king. What does he say? He says: drive the livestock into the fence. Why shall we drive it? The grass in the field is good. Our shepherds saw an army at the ford. How many men? They are many, and their horses are swift. Then we will drive it in, and the boys will guard the fence. I will tell the king.

Then let the warriors stand at the ford, and let the women and children sit in the wagons. The frost comes quickly. Then we will wait for the ice, and they will protect us.

plan.english: Young chief, what is the strength of a people? Its spears and its horses. Spears break, and horses run away. Then is it its cattle? Thieves steal cattle. Then tell me, wise one: what is it? The word that men keep. When a people keeps its oath, it does not fall. I will not break my oath.

plan.english: Of-True-Fame, both our herds seek this land. Our grandfathers fought here. Shall we two fight, or shall we divide it? Let us divide it. You take the half by the stream, and I will take the half by the mountain. And who will guard the boundary between us? Our shepherds. Let them give a pledge. At the full moon let us two eat a feast.
